statement: Which of these words, written in capital letters, has an up-and-down line of symmetry, so its left half is a mirror image of its right half?

choices.misconception: I thought any word that reads the same backwards has a mirror line, but the letter N itself is not symmetric up and down.
I saw that D and E each have a line of symmetry, but their lines go across, not up and down.
I checked that every letter has an up-and-down mirror line, but the word does not read the same backwards.
I thought S has a mirror line because it looks the same after a half turn, but turning is not the same as reflecting.

hints: Two things must both be true for the whole word to have a mirror line.
For an up-and-down mirror line through the middle, the word must read the same backwards, and every single letter must be symmetric about an up-and-down line. Check both for each word.
T and O are both symmetric about an up-and-down line. N, D, E and S are not.

solutions.reliable: A mirror line down the middle swaps the first letter with the last, the second with the second last, and so on, and also flips each letter. So two things are needed: the word reads the same backwards, and each letter has its own up-and-down mirror line. NOON reads the same backwards, but N is not symmetric up and down. DEED reads the same backwards, but D and E only have across lines. OHIO has symmetric letters, but backwards it reads OIHO. SOS: S has no mirror line at all. TOOT reads the same backwards, and T and O are each symmetric up and down. So TOOT works. The transferable idea: the symmetry of a whole shape needs the symmetry of its parts and of their arrangement.

whyOnTest: It probes the difference between a line of symmetry, a half-turn and a word that reads the same backwards.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
